# Need panel viewport mapping. Let's reconstruct: find panel position from svg grid lines? 
# Instead check monotonic consistency: map built x,y to device coords via a linear fit using several circles.
# Take first 600 circles as panel points in built order.
svg <- readLines("figure.svg", warn = FALSE)
idx <- grep("<circle", svg)
pat <- "cx='([-0-9.]+)' cy='([-0-9.]+)'"

cents <- do.call(rbind, lapply(m, function(x) as.numeric(x[2:3])))
colnames(cents) <- c("cx", "cy")
panel <- cents[1:600, ]
# fit cx = a + b*x ; cy = c + d*y (y flipped)
fitx <- lm(panel[,1] ~ b$x)
fity <- lm(panel[,2] ~ b$y)
summary(fitx)$r.squared
summary(fity)$r.squared
coef(fitx); coef(fity)
# residual check
max(abs(resid(fitx)))
max(abs(resid(fity)))

attrs <- regmatches(lines, gregexpr("[xy]='[-0-9.]+'|width='[-0-9.]+'|height='[-0-9.]+'", lines))

  getv <- function(n) { s <- grep(paste0("^", n, "="), a, value=TRUE); if(length(s)) as.numeric(sub(".*='([-0-9.]+)'.*","\\1",s)) else NA }
  data.frame(i=i, x=getv("x"), y=getv("y"), w=getv("width"), h=getv("height"),
             fill = if (grepl("fill: (#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6})", lines[i])) sub(".*fill: (#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}).*","\\1",lines[i]) else NA)
}))

# compute centers
library(stringr)
nums <- str_match(rects, "x='([0-9.]+)' y='([0-9.]+)' width='([0-9.]+)' height='([0-9.]+)'")
keep <- !is.na(nums[,1])
df <- data.frame(idx = which(keep),
                 x = as.numeric(nums[keep,2]), y = as.numeric(nums[keep,3]),
                 w = as.numeric(nums[keep,4]), h = as.numeric(nums[keep,5]))
df$cx <- df$x + df$w/2
df$cy <- df$y + df$h/2
df$fill <- str_match(rects[keep], "fill: (#[0-9A-Fa-f]+|none)")[,2]
df$stroke <- str_match(rects[keep], "stroke: (#[0-9A-Fa-f]+|none)")[,2]
print(df, digits = 4)
cat("\nTarget center (100.03, 166.37)\n")
d <- sqrt((df$cx - 100.03)^2 + (df$cy - 166.37)^2)
print(cbind(df, dist = d)[order(d), ], digits = 4)

panel_right <- sum(as.numeric(gt$widths[1:pos$r]))

y_pt <- panel_top*72 + (bt$y - y.range[1])/(y.range[2]-y.range[1])*(panel_bottom-panel_top)*72

x.range <- rng$x.range; y.range <- rng$y.range
bt <- b$data[[1]]
gt <- ggplotGrob(p1)
pos <- gt$layout[gt$layout$name == "panel", ]
print(pos)
panel_left  <- sum(as.numeric(gt$widths[1:(pos$l-1)]))
panel_right <- sum(as.numeric(gt$widths[1:pos$r]))
panel_top    <- sum(as.numeric(gt$heights[1:(pos$t-1)]))
panel_bottom <- sum(as.numeric(gt$heights[1:pos$b]))

library(grid)
library(gtable)
library(ggplot2)

p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp)) + ggtitle('disp and mpg seems connected')

)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(

## ----install, eval=FALSE--------------------------------------------------------------------------
# # 1) Make sure Bioconductor is installed
# if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
# #   install.packages("BiocManager") # [bench: install call removed]

# # 2) Install crumblr and dependencies:
# # From Bioconductor
# # BiocManager::install("crumblr") # [bench: install call removed]

# ---- chunk 3 ----
## ----crumblr--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(crumblr)

# Load cell counts, clustering and metadata
# from Kang, et al. (2018) https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042
data(IFNCellCounts)

# Apply crumblr transformation
# cobj is an EList object compatable with limma workflow
# cobj$E stores transformed values
# cobj$weights stores precision weights
#    corresponding to the regularized inverse variance
cobj <- crumblr(df_cellCounts)

# ---- chunk 4 ----
## ----vp, fig.height=4, fig.width=6----------------------------------------------------------------
library(variancePartition)

# Partition variance into components for Subject (i.e. ind)
#   and stimulation status, and residual variation
form <- ~ (1 | ind) + (1 | StimStatus)
vp <- fitExtractVarPartModel(cobj, form, info)

# Plot variance fractions
fig.vp <- plotPercentBars(vp)
fig.vp

# ---- chunk 5 ----
## ----pca, fig.height=5, fig.width=5---------------------------------------------------------------
library(ggplot2)

# Perform PCA
# use crumblr::standardize() to get values with
# approximately equal sampling variance,
# which is a key property for downstream PCA and clustering analysis.
pca <- prcomp(t(standardize(cobj)))

# merge with metadata
df_pca <- merge(pca$x, info, by = "row.names")

# Plot PCA
#   color by Subject
# 	shape by Stimulated vs unstimulated
ggplot(df_pca, aes(PC1, PC2, color = as.character(ind), shape = StimStatus)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
  scale_color_discrete(name = "Subject") +
  xlab("PC1") +
  ylab("PC2")

# ---- chunk 6 ----
## ----hclust---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap(cobj$E)

# ---- chunk 7 ----
## ----dream----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use variancePartition workflow to analyze each cell type
# Perform regression on each cell type separately
#  then use eBayes to shrink residual variance
# Also compatible with limma::lmFit()
fit <- dream(cobj, ~ StimStatus + ind, info)
fit <- eBayes(fit)

# Extract results for each cell type
topTable(fit, coef = "StimStatusstim", number = Inf)

# ---- chunk 8 ----
## ----treeTest-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Perform multivariate test across the hierarchy
res <- treeTest(fit, cobj, hcl, coef = "StimStatusstim")

# Plot hierarchy and testing results
plotTreeTest(res)

# gloss bench figure tree-077
# source: crumblr (vignette)
# Frozen by bench/R/harvest.R: code up to the chosen figure; see meta.json.
# ---- chunk 1 ----
## ----setup, echo=FALSE, results="hide"------------------------------------------------------------
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  tidy = FALSE,
  cache = TRUE,
  echo = TRUE,
  dev = c("png", "pdf"),
  package.startup.message = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  error = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

options(width = 100)

# ---- chunk 2 ----
## ----install, eval=FALSE--------------------------------------------------------------------------
# # 1) Make sure Bioconductor is installed
# if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
# #   install.packages("BiocManager") # [bench: install call removed]
# }
# 
# # 2) Install crumblr and dependencies:
# # From Bioconductor
# # BiocManager::install("crumblr") # [bench: install call removed]

# ---- chunk 3 ----
## ----crumblr--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(crumblr)

# Load cell counts, clustering and metadata
# from Kang, et al. (2018) https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042
data(IFNCellCounts)

# Apply crumblr transformation
# cobj is an EList object compatable with limma workflow
# cobj$E stores transformed values
# cobj$weights stores precision weights
#    corresponding to the regularized inverse variance
cobj <- crumblr(df_cellCounts)

# ---- chunk 4 ----
## ----vp, fig.height=4, fig.width=6----------------------------------------------------------------
library(variancePartition)

# Partition variance into components for Subject (i.e. ind)
#   and stimulation status, and residual variation
form <- ~ (1 | ind) + (1 | StimStatus)
vp <- fitExtractVarPartModel(cobj, form, info)

# Plot variance fractions
fig.vp <- plotPercentBars(vp)
fig.vp

# ---- chunk 5 ----
## ----pca, fig.height=5, fig.width=5---------------------------------------------------------------
library(ggplot2)

# Perform PCA
# use crumblr::standardize() to get values with
# approximately equal sampling variance,
# which is a key property for downstream PCA and clustering analysis.
pca <- prcomp(t(standardize(cobj)))

# merge with metadata
df_pca <- merge(pca$x, info, by = "row.names")

# Plot PCA
#   color by Subject
# 	shape by Stimulated vs unstimulated
ggplot(df_pca, aes(PC1, PC2, color = as.character(ind), shape = StimStatus)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
  scale_color_discrete(name = "Subject") +
  xlab("PC1") +
  ylab("PC2")

# ---- chunk 6 ----
## ----hclust---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap(cobj$E)

# ---- chunk 7 ----
## ----dream----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use variancePartition workflow to analyze each cell type
# Perform regression on each cell type separately
#  then use eBayes to shrink residual variance
# Also compatible with limma::lmFit()
fit <- dream(cobj, ~ StimStatus + ind, info)
fit <- eBayes(fit)

# Extract results for each cell type
topTable(fit, coef = "StimStatusstim", number = Inf)

# ---- chunk 8 ----
## ----treeTest-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Perform multivariate test across the hierarchy
res <- treeTest(fit, cobj, hcl, coef = "StimStatusstim")

# Plot hierarchy and testing results
plotTreeTest(res)

# gloss bench figure tree-077
# source: crumblr (vignette)
# Frozen by bench/R/harvest.R: code up to the chosen figure; see meta.json.
# ---- chunk 1 ----
## ----setup, echo=FALSE, results="hide"------------------------------------------------------------
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  tidy = FALSE,
  cache = TRUE,
  echo = TRUE,
  dev = c("png", "pdf"),
  package.startup.message = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  error = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

options(width = 100)

# ---- chunk 2 ----
## ----install, eval=FALSE--------------------------------------------------------------------------
# # 1) Make sure Bioconductor is installed
# if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
# #   install.packages("BiocManager") # [bench: install call removed]
# }
# 
# # 2) Install crumblr and dependencies:
# # From Bioconductor
# # BiocManager::install("crumblr") # [bench: install call removed]

# ---- chunk 3 ----
## ----crumblr--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(crumblr)

# Load cell counts, clustering and metadata
# from Kang, et al. (2018) https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042
data(IFNCellCounts)

# Apply crumblr transformation
# cobj is an EList object compatable with limma workflow
# cobj$E stores transformed values
# cobj$weights stores precision weights
#    corresponding to the regularized inverse variance
cobj <- crumblr(df_cellCounts)

# ---- chunk 4 ----
## ----vp, fig.height=4, fig.width=6----------------------------------------------------------------
library(variancePartition)

# Partition variance into components for Subject (i.e. ind)
#   and stimulation status, and residual variation
form <- ~ (1 | ind) + (1 | StimStatus)
vp <- fitExtractVarPartModel(cobj, form, info)

# Plot variance fractions
fig.vp <- plotPercentBars(vp)
fig.vp

# ---- chunk 5 ----
## ----pca, fig.height=5, fig.width=5---------------------------------------------------------------
library(ggplot2)

# Perform PCA
# use crumblr::standardize() to get values with
# approximately equal sampling variance,
# which is a key property for downstream PCA and clustering analysis.
pca <- prcomp(t(standardize(cobj)))

# merge with metadata
df_pca <- merge(pca$x, info, by = "row.names")

# Plot PCA
#   color by Subject
# 	shape by Stimulated vs unstimulated
ggplot(df_pca, aes(PC1, PC2, color = as.character(ind), shape = StimStatus)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
  scale_color_discrete(name = "Subject") +
  xlab("PC1") +
  ylab("PC2")

# ---- chunk 6 ----
## ----hclust---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap(cobj$E)

# ---- chunk 7 ----
## ----dream----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use variancePartition workflow to analyze each cell type
# Perform regression on each cell type separately
#  then use eBayes to shrink residual variance
# Also compatible with limma::lmFit()
fit <- dream(cobj, ~ StimStatus + ind, info)
fit <- eBayes(fit)

# Extract results for each cell type
topTable(fit, coef = "StimStatusstim", number = Inf)

# ---- chunk 8 ----
## ----treeTest-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Perform multivariate test across the hierarchy
res <- treeTest(fit, cobj, hcl, coef = "StimStatusstim")

# Plot hierarchy and testing results
plotTreeTest(res)

## ----crumblr--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(crumblr)

# Load cell counts, clustering and metadata
# from Kang, et al. (2018) https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042
data(IFNCellCounts)

# Apply crumblr transformation
# cobj is an EList object compatable with limma workflow
# cobj$E stores transformed values

cobj <- crumblr(df_cellCounts)

## ----vp, fig.height=4, fig.width=6----------------------------------------------------------------

# 	shape by Stimulated vs unstimulated
ggplot(df_pca, aes(PC1, PC2, color = as.character(ind), shape = StimStatus)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +

## ----setup, echo=FALSE, results="hide"------------------------------------------------------------
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  tidy = FALSE,

## ----install, eval=FALSE--------------------------------------------------------------------------
# # 1) Make sure Bioconductor is installed

# # From Bioconductor
# # BiocManager::install("crumblr") # [bench: install call removed]

# ---- chunk 3 ----
## ----crumblr--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(crumblr)

# Load cell counts, clustering and metadata
# from Kang, et al. (2018) https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042
data(IFNCellCounts)

# Apply crumblr transformation
# cobj is an EList object compatable with limma workflow
# cobj$E stores transformed values
# cobj$weights stores precision weights
#    corresponding to the regularized inverse variance
cobj <- crumblr(df_cellCounts)

# ---- chunk 4 ----
## ----vp, fig.height=4, fig.width=6----------------------------------------------------------------
library(variancePartition)

# Partition variance into components for Subject (i.e. ind)
#   and stimulation status, and residual variation
form <- ~ (1 | ind) + (1 | StimStatus)
vp <- fitExtractVarPartModel(cobj, form, info)

# Plot variance fractions
fig.vp <- plotPercentBars(vp)
fig.vp

# ---- chunk 5 ----
## ----pca, fig.height=5, fig.width=5---------------------------------------------------------------
library(ggplot2)

# Perform PCA
# use crumblr::standardize() to get values with
# approximately equal sampling variance,
# which is a key property for downstream PCA and clustering analysis.
pca <- prcomp(t(standardize(cobj)))

# merge with metadata
df_pca <- merge(pca$x, info, by = "row.names")

# Plot PCA
#   color by Subject
# 	shape by Stimulated vs unstimulated
ggplot(df_pca, aes(PC1, PC2, color = as.character(ind), shape = StimStatus)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
  scale_color_discrete(name = "Subject") +
  xlab("PC1") +
  ylab("PC2")

# ---- chunk 6 ----
## ----hclust---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap(cobj$E)

# ---- chunk 7 ----
## ----dream----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use variancePartition workflow to analyze each cell type
# Perform regression on each cell type separately
#  then use eBayes to shrink residual variance
# Also compatible with limma::lmFit()
fit <- dream(cobj, ~ StimStatus + ind, info)
fit <- eBayes(fit)

# Extract results for each cell type
topTable(fit, coef = "StimStatusstim", number = Inf)

# ---- chunk 8 ----
## ----treeTest-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Perform multivariate test across the hierarchy
res <- treeTest(fit, cobj, hcl, coef = "StimStatusstim")

# Plot hierarchy and testing results
plotTreeTest(res)

# gloss bench figure tree-077
# source: crumblr (vignette)
# Frozen by bench/R/harvest.R: code up to the chosen figure; see meta.json.
# ---- chunk 1 ----
## ----setup, echo=FALSE, results="hide"------------------------------------------------------------
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  tidy = FALSE,
  cache = TRUE,
  echo = TRUE,
  dev = c("png", "pdf"),
  package.startup.message = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,

  warning = FALSE
)

# ---- chunk 2 ----
## ----install, eval=FALSE--------------------------------------------------------------------------
# # 1) Make sure Bioconductor is installed
# if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
# #   install.packages("BiocManager") # [bench: install call removed]
# }
# 
# # 2) Install crumblr and dependencies:
# # From Bioconductor
# # BiocManager::install("crumblr") # [bench: install call removed]

# ---- chunk 3 ----
## ----crumblr--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(crumblr)

# Load cell counts, clustering and metadata
# from Kang, et al. (2018) https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042
data(IFNCellCounts)

# Apply crumblr transformation
# cobj is an EList object compatable with limma workflow
# cobj$E stores transformed values
# cobj$weights stores precision weights
#    corresponding to the regularized inverse variance
cobj <- crumblr(df_cellCounts)

# ---- chunk 4 ----
## ----vp, fig.height=4, fig.width=6----------------------------------------------------------------
library(variancePartition)

# Partition variance into components for Subject (i.e. ind)
#   and stimulation status, and residual variation
form <- ~ (1 | ind) + (1 | StimStatus)
vp <- fitExtractVarPartModel(cobj, form, info)

# Plot variance fractions
fig.vp <- plotPercentBars(vp)
fig.vp

# ---- chunk 5 ----
## ----pca, fig.height=5, fig.width=5---------------------------------------------------------------
library(ggplot2)

# Perform PCA
# use crumblr::standardize() to get values with
# approximately equal sampling variance,
# which is a key property for downstream PCA and clustering analysis.
pca <- prcomp(t(standardize(cobj)))

# merge with metadata
df_pca <- merge(pca$x, info, by = "row.names")

# Plot PCA
#   color by Subject
# 	shape by Stimulated vs unstimulated
ggplot(df_pca, aes(PC1, PC2, color = as.character(ind), shape = StimStatus)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
  scale_color_discrete(name = "Subject") +
  xlab("PC1") +
  ylab("PC2")

# ---- chunk 6 ----
## ----hclust---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap(cobj$E)

# ---- chunk 7 ----
## ----dream----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use variancePartition workflow to analyze each cell type
# Perform regression on each cell type separately
#  then use eBayes to shrink residual variance
# Also compatible with limma::lmFit()
fit <- dream(cobj, ~ StimStatus + ind, info)
fit <- eBayes(fit)

# Extract results for each cell type
topTable(fit, coef = "StimStatusstim", number = Inf)

# ---- chunk 8 ----
## ----treeTest-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Perform multivariate test across the hierarchy
res <- treeTest(fit, cobj, hcl, coef = "StimStatusstim")

# Plot hierarchy and testing results
plotTreeTest(res)
